Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:34: And the proof of this, from the passage concerning that wicked man, who said (Genesis 34:19), "and the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in Jacob's daughter" - and the delight in her was because she was the daughter of a great man, Jacob our father, peace be upon him; for a person should not delay performing a commandment and completing it, even though he knows that harm may come to him - as with that wicked man, for even though the matter touched his body and soul in the matter of circumcision, which is almost dangerous, he did not delay to do the thing, because of his delight in Jacob's daughter, as we explained. So too a person should not delay performing a commandment, because of his desire and delight in it - for every single commandment is "the daughter of Jacob," as is known, for within it are included the 248 commandments, and every single commandment is included of 248 [limbs/aspects], as I explained above - it follows that every commandment is a complete stature [komah].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:35: And when he considers the reality of the commandment, in the One who commands it, and the speed of performing the commandment in its execution, and that he not delay in performing it - this indicates the abundance of desire he has for it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:36: And therefore he must free himself from all worldly affairs and from all his thoughts, so that the will of his soul grows strong within him, and his soul cleaves to and is inflamed in its performance, to the point that even if he were given all the money in the world, he would not stop performing it - and just as it is unthinkable that a person would delay uniting with his wife, when his ultimate desire is for her, even if he were given all the money in the world - so it is fitting that his ultimate desire be for the commandment, because in its performance he unites with the daughter of the King, who is the Shechinah, the daughter of Jacob - "every wife is her husband's daughter" [a term applied], as it is said of Mordechai (Esther 2:7), "Mordechai took her for his own daughter." And it is not fitting to delay the union, but rather he should strive with speed and great alacrity in performing the commandment, and thereby he cleaves to the supernal life, and his soul shines with the illumination of the supernal light that shines in the performance of that commandment. And we will further elaborate below, with God's help, hinting at the virtue of the commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:37: And for the reason mentioned, you will find it does not say "for his soul delighted [chafetz nafsho] in Jacob's daughter," as it says above (Genesis 34:8), "for the soul of Shechem my son desires [chashkah]," and likewise "and his soul cleaved" - because here he was giving over his soul and body, therefore it says "delighted" [chafetz] without qualification, which encompasses everything.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:38: And in the cleaving of this great desire, a person must have desire for the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah - and this is the matter of "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might" (Deuteronomy 6:5). And Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains that "and you shall love the LORD your God" is said concerning love of the Shechinah; in these words (Zohar, Terumah 155b): he opened and said (Psalms 119:126), "it is time to act for the LORD; they have made void Your Torah" - "it is time to act for the LORD" - there is a "time" and there is a "time," (Ecclesiastes 3:8), "a time to love and a time to hate" - "time" is above: that "time" is the secret of faith, and it is called "a time of favor" - and this is what a person is obligated to love the LORD always, as it is said, "and you shall love the LORD your God" - and therefore "a time to love" is a time when a person is obligated to love; and there is another "time," which is the secret of "other gods," and a person is obligated to hate it and not let his heart be drawn after it - and this is "a time to hate" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:39: And so he further explains in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Terumah 158b), when Rashbi, peace be upon him, praises Moses our teacher, peace be upon him: you have upheld, concerning the Shechinah, "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart" - this is the body; "and with all your soul" - this is the soul, which has five names: neshamah, ruach, nefesh, chayah, yechidah; "and with all your might" - with all your wealth. The Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah will not depart from you through all of these. You considered that even if all the worlds were under your authority, you would give them to establish the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, and to make Him king with His Shechinah over all the officers of the nations of the world, and afterward to raise Him and His Shechinah in your own image, encompassing all good attributes, and in all the worlds and in the supernal and lower camps and over all Israel - the Holy One, blessed be He, joins a good thought to a deed; after you were created, whatever you thought toward your Master will be fulfilled through you, and it will never depart from you, but rather you will be in His image in everything - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:40: Further, in the Tikkunim (37a), in these words: and the gift for the Shechinah must be made from that which is precious to him, as the masters of the Mishnah established: "and you shall love the LORD" with what is precious to you - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:41: And they explain, of blessed memory (Berachot 61b): there is a person to whom his body is more precious than his wealth, therefore it says "with all your soul"; and vice versa, "with all your might" - that a person should hold the Holy One, blessed be He, dear with what is more precious to him. And they explain this discourse in the Tikkunim (141a), in these words: there is fear and there is love. There is one who fears the Holy One, blessed be He, so that his children be favored, or so that he not come down to poverty, or who loves Him because He gives him wealth and tests him - "now let us do so and see whether the LORD is among us and gives us reward for it - if not" - for if He does not give him reward for it, he does not love Him, nor give charity, nor perform a commandment; and he certainly tests the Holy One, blessed be He - this is among those bad mixtures of which it is said (Exodus 17:7), "is the LORD among us, or not?" Rather, complete love and fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, is whether He gives him reward with goodness or does not give it to him; and therefore the Torah counted (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might" - and the earlier ones established: if your soul is more precious to you than your wealth, therefore it says "with all your soul"; and if your wealth is more precious to you than your soul, therefore it says "with all your might." A person who performs all the commandments and prays, but they give him no reward for them - had they given him reward for them, he would not have performed them - for certainly there are many people who are wealthy with abundant wealth, and they hold their wealth dearer than their soul, for the wealth of the soul is good deeds in the World to Come, and the wealth of the body is money and the pleasure of this world. And those who hold money dearer than the soul - even if the entire Torah were given to them for a hundred zuz, they would not give it for its sake, because money is more precious to them than the soul; and whoever fears and loves Him only for the sake of money, this one has made money his essential concern, and the Torah he loves for the Holy One, blessed be He's sake is secondary to him - this love and fear the Holy One, blessed be He, does not consider [valid].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:42: Rather, the essence of love and fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, is that even though he loves his money more than his soul, he loves Him with his money, in what he considers essential to him, and not with what is secondary to him - therefore it says "and with all your might." And likewise, one who considers his soul more precious than his money, and would give all the money in the world rather than be harmed in the smallest limb he has - therefore it says "with all your soul," with what he loves - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:43: And just as "chefetz" [delight] is found in the matter of performing the commandments, so it is found in engaging in the study of Torah - that the will of the soul grows strong within him, and all the senses of the body are nullified, and his soul cleaves to the contemplation of Torah until he feels nothing of the matters of this world - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say in the Gemara (Shabbat 88a), concerning Rava, who was so absorbed in study that a certain [official] sat down upon his hand, and blood flowed from his fingernails, and he did not feel the blood flowing from him, because of his abundant absorption in Torah. And so I have heard of several later sages who had this great cleaving to Torah, to the point that they felt nothing of the matters of this world at all. For just as one who desires his beloved nullifies all his other thoughts while desiring her, and the fire of her love burns in his heart, until he eats and drinks and sleeps with all his thoughts on his beloved - so a person should have love of the Creator, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:44: And so we learn from an incident that Rabbi Yitzchak of Acre, of blessed memory, wrote: he said, that one day the king's daughter came out of the bathhouse, and a man of the idle street-corner sitters saw her, and sighed a great sigh, and said, would that she were in my power, to do with her as I please. And the king's daughter answered and said to him: it will be in the graveyard, and not here. When he heard these words of hers, he rejoiced, for he thought she had told him to go to the graveyard and sit there, and she would come to him and he would do with her as he pleased. But she did not intend this; rather, she meant to say that there, specifically, the small and the great, the young and the old, the lowly and the honored, are equal - "the small and the great are there" (Job 3:19) - there all are equal; but here, no - for it is unthinkable that a member of the common people approach a king's daughter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:45: And that man arose and went to the graveyard, and sat there and bound the thought of his mind to her, and always thought of her form; and out of his abundant desire for her, he stripped his thought of everything sensory and placed it entirely in the form of that woman and her beauty; and day and night he always sat in the graveyard, and there he ate and drank and there he slept, for he said, if she does not come today, she will come tomorrow - and so he did for many days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:46: And from his abundant abstinence from everything sensory, in binding the thought of his mind to one thing always, and his solitude and his complete desire, his soul was stripped of sensory things and returned to cleave to intellectual things, to the point that it was stripped of everything sensory, even of the woman, and cleaved to the Blessed Name - until, after a few days, it had stripped away everything sensory and desired the divine intellectual object, and he returned to being a complete servant, a holy man of God, until his prayer was heard and his blessing effective for all travelers who passed that way - merchants, horsemen, and foot travelers who passed that way would turn aside to him and receive his blessing, until his name spread far and wide - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:47: And he further elaborated there on the virtue of this ascetic, and Rabbi Yitzchak of Acre, peace be upon him, wrote there, in the tales of the ascetics, that one who has never desired a woman is comparable to a donkey, and lower than it - the reason being that one must, from the sensory, come to discern divine service, as we explained - and through this the meaning of the word "chefetz" is understood in its proper form.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:48: And from this incident we learn that whoever desires the Torah so greatly that, day and night, he thinks of nothing in the world but it, will certainly attain a wondrous level in his soul, and will not need self-mortifications and fasts - for cleaving depends only on desire and love of the Torah, to the point that he desires it as one desires his beloved, and also through the constancy of rising at midnight with desire, as explained in its place, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:1: This chapter explains the things that give birth to love, and I have seen fit to copy here what the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote on this matter (Gate of the Love of God, chapter 3), in these words: the author said: but what is the way to the love of God, blessed be He? I say, in answer to this question, that this request cannot be asked except after many preliminary preparations, and when these preparations are fulfilled, love of God, blessed be He, is born from them; but one who aims at it directly cannot attain it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:2: And the preparations that one should properly believe he must place first within his soul are: two unifications of the hearts, and two submissions, and two reckonings, and two contemplations. As for the two unifications of the hearts: one of them is to unify the heart in the unity of the Creator, and the second is to unify one's deeds for His sake, to serve Him for His honor alone. As for the two submissions: one of them is submission to God, blessed be He, and the second is submission to those who fear God and His chosen ones. As for the two reckonings: one of them is his reckoning with his soul concerning what he owes to God for the constancy of His goodness, and the second is his reckoning with his soul concerning His hiding of his sins, and His prolonging [His patience] for him, and His forgiveness. As for the two contemplations: one of them is contemplation of what happened to those who came before, standing upon the books of the prophets and the words of the ancients, as it is written (Psalms 143:5), "I remember the days of old"; and the second is contemplation of the world, in what he sees of the wonders of the Creator, blessed be He, in His creations. And I have already explained in this book general principles concerning this matter, to the extent of my ability, sufficient for one who understands and directs himself toward what will bring his salvation and deliverance in this world and the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:3: And when he establishes all this, and joins to it abstinence from the pleasures and desires of this world, and understands the greatness of the Creator and His essence and His truth, and realizes the smallness of the worth of his own soul, its insignificance and lowliness, and afterward recognizes the Creator's abundant goodness toward him and the greatness of His kindness with him - then love of God will come from the believer, close upon this, with a complete heart and the true purification of his soul, and his yearning for Him with effort, diligence, and alacrity, similar to what is said (Isaiah 26:9), "my soul desires You in the night," and it says (Psalms 42:3), "my soul thirsts for God" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:4: And concerning the matter of contemplation, I have seen fit also to copy his words in the Gate of Contemplation, chapter 1, which speaks of the general matters encompassing all the particulars of contemplation, in these words, in chapter 4, explaining several signs of wisdom in creatures that we can discern: we say that the aspects of wisdom established in creatures, in their many kinds and individuals, are seven. One of them is the sign of wisdom apparent in the roots and foundations of the world - in our seeing the earth standing in the middle, and the waters adjacent, above it, and the air adjacent to them, and the fire above, in a proportion and measure from which nothing changes - each one attending to its own place, unique to it and bounded for it; and the sea stands, and its waters are bound within it, not passing its boundary, even when its waves roar and its winds storm, as it is written (Job 38:10-11), "and I set My bound for it, and placed bars and doors, and said, thus far shall you come and no farther." And it says, concerning the standing of the heavens and the earth (Psalms 119:89-90), "forever, O LORD, Your word stands firm in the heavens; Your faithfulness is to all generations" - as King David, peace be upon him, composed on this matter in the psalm (Psalms 104:1), "bless the LORD, O my soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:5: And the second aspect is the sign of wisdom apparent in the human species, who is the microcosm, and so on - and to this King David, peace be upon him, alludes when he says (Psalms 8:2), "O LORD, our Master, how mighty is Your name in all the earth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:6: And the third is the sign of wisdom apparent in the composition of man and the joining of his body and the powers of his soul and the light of the intellect that the Creator singled out for him, giving him superiority over the rest of the non-speaking living creatures, and he is similar to the macrocosm, comparable to it in his roots and foundations. And to this Job alludes when he says (Job 10:10-12), "did You not pour me out like milk," and so on, "You clothed me with skin and flesh," and so on, "You have granted me life and kindness," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:7: And the fourth is the sign of wisdom apparent in the other kinds of living creatures, from the smallest to the greatest - among them the flying, the swimming, the crawling, and the four-legged - according to the division of their forms, their measures, their use, their benefit, and their status in the world, as mentioned in the passage where the Creator rebuked Job in order to arouse him (Job 38:41), "who provides food for the raven," and the rest of what is recounted there of the kinds of land and sea creatures.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:8: And the fifth is the sign of wisdom apparent in the plants and minerals prepared for the benefit of man, and the ways he benefits from them, according to the division of their natures, their compositions, and their properties - and the ancients already mentioned this matter in their books, to the extent of their understanding, as it is written (I Kings 5:13), "and he spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows out of the wall," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:9: And the sixth is the sign of wisdom apparent in the sciences and crafts and activities that the Creator, blessed be He, prepared for man for the completion of his welfare, and the causes of his allotted sustenance and his other general and individual benefits - and to this he alludes when he says (Job 38:36), "who has put wisdom in the hidden parts, or who has given understanding to the mind?" and he says (Proverbs 2:6), "for the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:10: And the seventh is the sign of wisdom apparent in the establishment of the Torah and the laws by which to serve the Creator, blessed be He, so that one who diligently attends to them attains, through them, the pleasures of this world immediately and the reward of the World to Come in the end - as Scripture says (Isaiah 55:2), "hearken diligently to Me, and eat what is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness," and it says, "incline your ear, and come to Me; hear, and your soul shall live." And upon this depend the matters of the leaders through whom the order of governance of the other nations and their welfare is arranged, and they stand for them in the place of the Torah in worldly matters alone; and it has already been said that the level of nature relative to the Torah is like the level of a servant relative to his master, for the powers of nature conduct the governance of the world according to what suits the Torah, as it is written (Exodus 23:25), "and you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water," and it says (ibid. 15:26), "and He said, if you will diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes," and so on, and many similar verses - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:11: And know that although what the pious teacher, author of Chovot HaLevavot, wrote is true - that contemplation of worldly matters is what arouses love - and for this reason we were compelled to copy his words concerning contemplation, so too, according to the secret, contemplation of worldly matters arouses love; and therefore we must elaborate on the matters of contemplation in order to arouse love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:12: And the reason is that the world endures only through Chesed, as the verse says (Psalms 89:3), "I have said, the world is built with kindness" - it is not written "was built" but "shall be built" [yibaneh, future/continuous tense] - for the world is built anew, every single day, through Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:13: And so they explain this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (30b), on the verse (Psalms 7:12), "and God is indignant [zo'em] every day"; in these words: "El" [God], in every place, is the abundant illumination of supernal wisdom, and it endures in its own existence; and were it not that this "El" is aroused in the world, the world could not endure even for one hour before the harsh judgments that are aroused in the world every day. This is what is written (Genesis 2:4), "these are the generations [toldot] of the heavens and the earth when they were created [behibaram]" - do not read "behibaram" but "beAvraham" [through Abraham] - through the arousal of Abraham they endure; and when Abraham is aroused in the world, all those judgments found every single day are pushed outside and do not stand before him - this is what is written, "and God is indignant every day" - it is not written "will be indignant" or "indignant [as an occasional state]," but "indignant every day" - every single day judgment is found, and it pushes it outside, and he [Abraham] endures and sweetens the world - this is what is written (Psalms 42:9), "by day the LORD commands His kindness" - and were it not for this, the world could not endure even for one moment, and therefore everything endures for Abraham's sake - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:14: And through this discourse we may understand what we say in the Yotzer blessing, "and in His goodness He renews the work of creation every single day continually" - for "goodness" [tov] is the secret of the known Chesed, and the light of Chesed, flowed every day to renew all the existing things in the world and give them endurance, is the "renewal" - similar to the moon, renewed from the light of the sun. And this is what we say, as stated: "who makes lights," and so on - and the intent is that the verse informs us of the matter of renewal by saying "who makes [oseh] lights" - meaning that He is always making great lights, for the reason that "His kindness is forever," for Chesed is what renews them and makes them anew every day; and for this reason the verse does not say that He "made" [asah] great lights, which would imply the past, at the time of the world's creation, but rather "who makes" [oseh] - meaning that every single day He makes and renews. And this is also "who makes new things" [oseh chadashot], said in the Yotzer blessing, "El Baruch" - and this corresponds to Chesed, for so we find it said (Isaiah 52:3 [an allusion]), "the kindness of God all day."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:15: And it is possible that in order for us to remember that His goodness is renewed every day - which indicates that He, blessed be He, created the world from nothing and renews it every day - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, instituted matters of the blessings using "Name" and "Kingship": YHVH - because He brings existing things into being; and "King" - because He watches over them, like a king who watches over and has mercy on his servants; so the Holy One, blessed be He, watches over the world, since He created it, to give it endurance and standing forever, so that His flow never ceases from the world for a moment, and the light is always renewed in proportion to the ongoing chain [of existence]. And we say "who creates the fruit of," and so on - the intent is also along these lines: that were it not for His flow, flowed for the endurance of existing things, that fruit, or that matter, would not have been created - for were it not for the water and dew that descend every day, the world would have no endurance; and likewise the shining of the sun to sweeten the fruits of the tree, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:14), "and with the precious things of the fruits of the sun, and with the precious things of the yield of the moons" - for there are fruits in the world that ripen through the sun and some through the moon, and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, causes the sun and moon to shine every day, the world could not endure. If so, through them the work of creation is renewed, and every day the Holy One, blessed be He, creates the world anew - and to this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, instituted in the Yotzer blessing, "who renews in His goodness, every day continually," and so on; and so too the matter of "Yotzer HaMe'orot" [who forms the lights], for through them is the renewal of the world and the work of creation - and the whole matter of renewal is from the side of Chesed, which is what renews it, as we explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:16: And in the Tikkunim (145a), it says that the sun first emerges red and afterward turns white; in these words: and because it first draws from Gevurah, the sun emerges red; afterward it clothes itself in Chesed, which is white, and through it the sun's wrath is calmed - to this point. And this distinction, too, is among the distinctions the discerning reader must discern in the creation of the world, as we shall explain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:17: And also the reality of the creation of several things in the world that sustain the entire world all come through Chesed - and several things that King David, peace be upon him, mentioned in the Great Hallel psalm, concerning the flowing of springs, living water, day and night without ceasing - and the water is drawn from the side of Chesed, and for the sustaining of the world, Chesed flows without interruption and descends below. And fire is in between, because it is judgment, ascending above everything, for a small amount of it suffices. And air is in between, and everything is made and arranged in the order of His supernal attributes, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:18: And so too what is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va'era (24a), that the south is arid and dry from the side of heat, and the north is moist with water - and it would seem that it should be the reverse, for "out of the north evil breaks forth," and there it would seem that fire and heat should be. And they answer that the Holy One, blessed be He, mixes them - and we will copy some of his text below. And fire, from this aspect, is mercy - for when the waters freeze on the north side, they are released and flow from the south side because of this fire - and through this the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Bereshit 29b) are understood; and so, at the time of cold, fire is mercy and kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:19: And along these lines is the matter of the shining of the sun and the blowing of the winds, as explained in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 28:11): Rabbi Levi and the Rabbis [disagreed]. Rabbi Levi says: whatever creatures raise up through commandments and good deeds in this world suffices for the Holy One, blessed be He, to make the sun shine for them, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:5), "and the sun rises and the sun sets." And the Rabbis say: whatever the righteous raise up through commandments and good deeds in this world suffices for the Holy One, blessed be He, to renew their faces like the disc of the sun, as it is said (Judges 5:31), "and those who love Him are as the sun going forth in its might." Rabbi Yannai said: it is the way of the world that a person takes one pound of meat from the market - how much labor he labors, how much distress he suffers, until he cooks it! But people sleep on their beds, and the Holy One, blessed be He, brings back the winds, and raises the clouds, and grows the plants, and ripens the fruits, and they give only the payment of the Omer - this is what is written (Leviticus 23:10), "and you shall bring the sheaf of the first of your harvest to the priest" - to this point. And they further elaborate there on the virtue of the wind, to dry out the land in the rainy season and winnow the straw so that the wheat be clean; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:20: Behold, all these matters and the like are all on the side of Chesed - and therefore it says in the discourse I copied, that the Holy One, blessed be He, grows plants, and so on, and they give only the Omer to the priest - and it is known that the priest is Chesed, "Your Tummim and Urim are with Your pious one" (Deuteronomy 33:8) - and the intent is that since everything comes from the side of Chesed, one should bring the "first" close to Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:21: And so too, several matters that King David, peace be upon him, mentioned in the Great Hallel psalm, which contains twenty-six [instances of] "for His kindness is forever" (Psalms 136): "to Him who made the heavens with understanding, for His kindness is forever," and so on; "to Him who spread the earth above the waters, for His kindness is forever"; "the sun to rule by day, for His kindness is forever"; "the moon and stars," and so on; and several other miracles mentioned in the psalm, all through Chesed: "to Him who struck Egypt," and so on, "to Him who divided the Red Sea into parts," and so on, "to Him who led His people through the wilderness," and so on. And if we were to elaborate in explaining each and every one of them, we would depart from the intent of this exposition, and our wish is only to arouse the exposition alone, so that a person may weigh and discern His kindness, blessed be He, performing so many acts with us - and through this he will cleave to the side of His kindness, being a lover; for the lover cleaves to the side of Chesed, as explained in chapter 2, as it is written (Isaiah 41:8), "the seed of Abraham My beloved," and it is said (Psalms 31:24), "love the LORD, all you His pious ones," and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:22: And therefore we must explain, concerning the matter of contemplation, three general categories that encompass all the particulars of contemplation explained in Chovot HaLevavot: the first, contemplation of the world and its particulars - living creatures, animals, birds, and plants; and of the supernal ones - the firmaments, the sun and moon, and so on. The second, contemplation of the creation of man in general, and his governance from the day of his birth to the day of his death. The third, contemplation of the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel, and the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performs for them in general. And when a person discerns His kindnesses, blessed be He, in the particulars that will be explained, he will recognize and know that He is One, alone, and there is none else - that He brought them into existence and He sustains them - and this is that "ahavah" [love] adds up [in gematria] to "echad" [one]; and when he knows that He is One, he will cleave to His love properly. And this is why, in the third passage of the tefillin, which is "Shema Yisrael," they explain in Parashat Va'etchanan (Zohar 267a) that it corresponds to Chesed - in it the unity is mentioned, "the LORD our God, the LORD is one," and afterward the matter of love is mentioned, "and you shall love the LORD your God," and so on - for the essential service, to give over one's soul in love of one's Creator, cannot be directed toward Him except after knowing that He is One, alone, who created him for His honor, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:23: And these two functions specific to Chesed that I have explained - one, the sustaining of the world and its renewal through it, and the second, the matter of unity - Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Pekudin [portions], in the commandment of tefillin; in these words (Zohar, end of Bo, 43b): the third passage, "Shema" - this is the secret of the right side, called Chesed Elyon [Supernal Kindness], which unifies the unity of everything to the four directions, and the Holy One, blessed be He, arranges through it the order of the whole world - and this is what spreads in every direction, even within the lowest depths - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:24: Contemplation of the world in general - it is fitting to consider that this world was created through the 32 [paths of] "Elohim" mentioned in the account of creation, which are the thirty-two paths; and we have learned at the beginning of Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 1, mishnah 1): "with thirty-two wondrous paths of wisdom, Yah, YHVH Tzevaot, engraved His world." And although there are several interpretations of this mishnah, for our purposes the plain meaning suffices: that through the thirty-two paths of wisdom came the creation of all existing things in the world. And this is what the verse says (Psalms 104:24), "how many are Your works, O LORD! You have made them all in wisdom," and so on - it follows that the power of His wisdom, blessed be He, spread into all existing things to give them endurance, and every single plant and animal and beast has an angel and a supernal spiritual force - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Bereshit Rabbah 10:6), on "do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you establish their dominion over the earth?" (Job 38:33) - there is not a single plant below that does not have a constellation [mazal] in the firmament that strikes it and says to it, grow! And this is the reason for [the prohibition of] kilayim [mixed species], as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (86b). And Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, peace be upon him, wrote that of this it is said (Genesis 1:11), "let the earth sprout vegetation, herb yielding seed after its kind" - "after its kind" literally, according to that power coming to it from above, from the particular species assigned to it. And so it is said of birds and fish (Genesis 1:21), "which the waters swarmed forth, after their kinds" - and this too is "after their kinds" literally, according to the flow of that species flowed upon it from heaven.
